document_title: The drones came first. Drone hubs in Round Rock and Rowlett
_note: Slide strings read off the render report's text nodes and each frame's own source line by build_copy.py.
caption:
Rowlett zoned for drone hubs. Round Rock hasn't.

May 20th, 2025. Rowlett's City Council voted 6 to 0 to add drone hubs to its zoning code. Zipline was the applicant. DroneXL reports the rule came before Zipline opened there.

October 9th. Zipline began taking orders in Round Rock, DroneXL reports. The city puts the hub in its extraterritorial jurisdiction near North Kenney Fort and Joe DiMaggio Boulevards. Its zoning doesn't specifically address drone hubs.

Now the city is working with Zipline toward an in-city hub behind Renaissance Square on Interstate 35. It says that site will help it write rules for future hubs. It routes operational feedback to Zipline and safety concerns to the FAA.

The deck weighs what Zipline says the aircraft decides against what the city still decides.

Which order serves neighbors better, the rule first or the hub first?

#RoundRock #Rowlett #Zipline

S1.headline: The drones came first
S1.body: Zipline began taking orders in Round Rock on October 9th, DroneXL reports. The City of Round Rock says its zoning ordinances don't specifically address drone delivery hubs. The aircraft is drawn to illustrate.

S2.headline: The first hub is outside city limits
S2.body: Round Rock places the facility near North Kenney Fort and Joe DiMaggio Boulevards, in its extraterritorial jurisdiction. Citing the company, the city says service reaches eligible customers within three miles. The tower and aircraft are drawn to illustrate.
strings: The first hub is outside city limits

Round Rock places the facility near North Kenney Fort and Joe DiMaggio Boulevards, in its extraterritorial jurisdiction. Citing the company, the city says service reaches eligible customers within three miles. The tower and aircraft are drawn to illustrate.

S3.headline: The city can't regulate the flight path
S3.body: Round Rock says the FAA regulates airspace and flight paths. Its page says drones may fly over residential areas on approved routes. Inside city limits it may regulate where drone infrastructure sits. The aircraft is drawn to illustrate.

S4.headline: Three miles from the hub
S4.body: Citing the company, the city says service reaches within three miles of the hub. A circle that wide covers about 28.3 square miles, computed here. The ring is drawn to illustrate.

S5.headline: Zipline says the aircraft decides
S5.body: The company says each aircraft reserves its own route before launch, avoids other aircraft with an onboard system and responds to problems on its own. Every claim here is Zipline's. The aircraft and tower are drawn to illustrate.
strings: The company says each aircraft reserves its own route before launch, avoids other aircraft with an onboard system and responds to problems on its own. Every claim here is Zipline's. The aircraft and tower are drawn to illustrate.

S6.headline: People watch from somewhere else
S6.body: Zipline says trained staff monitor its flights from a remote operations center. The room is drawn to illustrate.
strings: Zipline says trained staff monitor its flights from a remote operations center. The room is drawn to illustrate.

S7.headline: Rowlett wrote the rule first, DroneXL reports
S7.body: Rowlett's minutes record a 6 to 0 vote adding drone hubs and kiosks to its zoning code on May 20th, 2025. Zipline was the applicant. In the minutes a member says the hub's special use permit "is the control." The chamber is drawn with one microphone per vote cast.

S8.headline: The neighbor gets an email address
S8.body: Round Rock directs operational feedback to Zipline at community@zipline.com and safety concerns to the FAA. Citing Community Impact, DroneXL reports a limit of about 5 pounds per order, lowered on a tether. The pod and yard are drawn to illustrate.

S9.headline: Next, the hub comes before the rule
S9.body: Round Rock is working with Zipline toward a hub behind Renaissance Square on northbound Interstate 35. The city says that site will help it develop regulations for future facilities inside city limits. Drawn to illustrate.
